scenario: [LNUL.4.10] for the arguments of a builtin call: when two arguments fault, the call yields the fault [LNUL.4.2]'s order selects, and an argument's position never enters. The builtin is `max` (two Int arguments, [LEXP.3.8]); one argument is `p.a // p.z`, which traps (DIVIDE_BY_ZERO), the other `len(p.body.obj)`, `len` of a Json object rather than an array, which raises a TypeError ([LEXP.6.2]). The kind order ranks the TypeError first. Two rules put the trap in each argument position, so a runtime that yields the FIRST argument's fault (or records both) fails at least one. Its twin LNUL.4.10.builtin_trap_beside_a_type_error_records_no_trap pins that the trap is not recorded ([LERR.1.4.11]). Path: the CALL argument loop -- libds rete/eval.c eval_call (each argument evaluated with faults held, ds_rete_held_select), Mercury ds.eval.m eval_all (folded with ds.fault.lnul_4_2_yielded). No adapter is involved: `max` and `len` are builtins of both runtimes.
rules_ds:
schema Payload scope logical:
    body: Json key
    a: Int mutable
    z: Int mutable

rule trap_first:
    Payload p where max(p.a // p.z, len(p.body.obj)) > 0
->
    log info "first"

rule trap_second:
    Payload p where max(len(p.body.obj), p.a // p.z) > 0
->
    log info "second"
